cleanIntro: This guide follows Mauser's manual for the Mauser 12 family; check your variant against it. The Mauser 12 is a turn-bolt repeater with a detachable magazine and a 3-position safety on the bolt shroud: forward dot is Safe with the bolt locked, the middle dot is safe but lets the bolt open, and F is Fire. Mauser's strip is short and exact — magazine out, bolt out past the bolt catch, and the bolt safety shroud off the bolt for cleaning. The book goes no further than that.

steps.title: Read the barrel: this book is for the Mauser 12
steps.action: This guide follows Mauser's manual for the Mauser 12 family; check your variant against it. Mauser tells the owner to confirm they have the right instructions by reading the model designation and the caliber off the left side of the barrel, on the chamber. The M12 Extreme is not named in the book, which says only that equipment varies by variant.
steps.prose: Everything that follows is the Mauser 12 procedure as Mauser prints it, stated as generally as the book states it. If your rifle carries something the book does not describe, this guide does not cover that part.
steps.quote: the caliber are indicated on the left side of the barrel
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — General Safety Instructions, p.18

steps.title: Safety to the middle dot
steps.action: Muzzle in a safe direction, finger outside the trigger guard. Move the safety lever with thumb and index finger to the central position, the white middle dot. In that position the rifle is safe and cannot be fired, but the bolt can be opened — on the forward dot the bolt is locked shut.
steps.prose: Mauser warns against having a finger inside the trigger guard while working the safety catch: it can cause an involuntary discharge. The middle dot is the unloading position because it is the only safe position that lets the bolt move.
steps.quote: Set the safety lever to the central position as described under 4.3.
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 7. Unloading, p.23

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Press the magazine release button at the bottom of the receiver and take the magazine out. Do this before you open the bolt, so the bolt does not feed another round from it.
steps.prose: The magazine is marked on its side with its type and the calibers it takes; keep it with the rifle it belongs to.
steps.quote: Press the magazine release button at the bottom of the receiver and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 3.2. Removing the magazine, p.20

steps.title: Open the bolt and empty the chamber
steps.action: Swivel the bolt handle up and pull the bolt back. A chambered cartridge is extracted and ejected as the bolt comes back. Then empty any cartridges still in the magazine, and look into the chamber to see it is empty.
steps.prose: Mauser's general rule: treat the rifle as loaded until you have opened the bolt and checked the chamber yourself. If a cartridge ever fails to fire, the book says to wait about 60 seconds, muzzle in a safe direction, before opening the bolt.
steps.quote: At the same time, the cartridge is extracted from the chamber and ejected.
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 7. Unloading, p.23

steps.title: Remove the bolt past the bolt catch
steps.action: Safety still on the middle dot, bolt handle up, pull the open bolt all the way back. Push the bolt catch on the left side down and hold it there with your left hand, and at the same time draw the bolt out to the rear with your right.
steps.prose: The bolt stops at the catch; it is not stuck. If it will not come out, the catch is not held fully down.
steps.quote: Push the bolt catch down and hold it in this position with your left hand.
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 1.2. Removing the bolt, p.20

steps.title: Take the bolt safety shroud off the bolt
steps.action: With the safety on the middle dot and the bolt out, press and hold the protruding pin on the left side of the bolt. Using the indentation in the steel (the nose), turn the bolt safety shroud about 4 mm toward the bolt handle (to the right), then pull the shroud back off the bolt.
steps.prose: ⛔ Mauser's caution: once the shroud is off, the safety must never be moved from the central position. And the shroud comes off for cleaning only — this is not a part to remove for any other reason.
steps.quote: If the bolt safety shroud is removed, the safety must never be moved from the central position.
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 2.1. Removing the bolt safety shroud — CAUTION, p.20

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Magazine out, bolt out of the receiver, bolt safety shroud off the bolt. That is the whole strip Mauser publishes for the Mauser 12.
steps.prose: The barrel, chamber and receiver are now open from the rear, and the bolt, shroud and magazine are in your hands for cleaning. The stock bolts appear in the parts list but the book gives no procedure for taking the stock off — it stays on.
steps.quote: Remove the bolt safety shroud piece for cleaning purposes only
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 2. Removing and Inserting the Bolt Safety Shroud — IMPORTANT, p.20

steps.title: Clean the bore and chamber after every firing
steps.action: After firing, clean the barrel and conserve it — work from the open rear now that the bolt is out. Give the chamber particular attention. Where ammunition residue can clearly be seen, Mauser recommends cleaning the barrel chemically, then wiping the barrel and especially the chamber dry and oiling them.
steps.prose: Powder residue draws moisture, and the chamber gets hand sweat carried in on every cartridge, which can react and cause corrosion. Follow the cleaning product maker's instructions and warnings.
steps.quote: as the powder residues in the chamber and barrel will attract moisture
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 11. Care and Maintenance — Bore, p.24

steps.title: Dry the chamber and bore before you shoot
steps.action: The oil that conserves the bore in storage has to come out before the rifle is fired: free the chamber and barrel of oil and dry them before use.
steps.prose: Oil left in the chamber or barrel shifts the point of impact on the first shot. Mauser also says not to store the rifle with a sealed muzzle or a muzzle protector.
steps.quote: We strongly advise that the chamber and barrel be freed of oil and dried before use
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 11. Care and Maintenance — Bore, p.24

steps.title: Metal parts clean and lightly oiled
steps.action: Wipe the barrel exterior, the action, the bolt and its shroud, and keep every metal part clean with a thin coat of suitable gun oil. A barrel that is damp or has sweated in a synthetic case gets wiped dry and lightly oiled.
steps.prose: The blued barrel surface resists scratches and corrosion with correct care, but Mauser says that protection cannot be guaranteed completely. Stock preservative is not for metal.
steps.quote: Keep all metal parts of the rifle clean and slightly oiled at all times.
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 11. Care and Maintenance — Metal parts, p.24

steps.title: ⛔ No oil or grease into the trigger or action
steps.action: Keep oil and grease out of the trigger mechanism and the action while you clean. Then, unloaded and with the safety on the forward dot, check the trigger moves smoothly.
steps.prose: Mauser's caution: under some conditions oil and grease resinify — harden — and that can cause dangerous malfunctions. Gummy oil or dirt in the trigger is exactly what the smooth-movement check is there to catch. Mauser also asks that the rifle be checked by an authorized dealer before each hunting season or trip.
steps.quote: care must be taken to ensure that no oil or grease leaks into the trigger
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 11. Care and Maintenance — CAUTION, p.24

steps.title: Stock care products on wood, never gun oil
steps.action: Mauser's wooden stocks are oil finished: treat them regularly with good quality stock care products. Leave gun oil off the stock. For the scope, follow the optics maker's own care instructions.
steps.prose: The two products are not interchangeable in either direction — stock preservative is not for metal, and gun oil is not for the stock.
steps.quote: Gun oil is not suitable for stock care.
steps.cite: Mauser 12 bolt action rifle — Operating Instructions — UNKNOWN — read off the manual's own pages — 11. Care and Maintenance — Stocks, p.24

deepAbsentReason: Mauser's Mauser 12 manual ends at the field strip: its only disassembly is removing the magazine (§3.2), the bolt (§1.2) and the bolt safety shroud, which it says comes off for cleaning purposes only (§2, p.20). The stock bolts are listed among the main components (p.17) but the book gives no stock-removal or further disassembly procedure, and its care section (pp.24–25) closes by asking for the rifle to be checked by an authorized dealer before each hunting season or trip.

reassembly: Bolt safety shroud: slide it into the bolt, press and hold the pin, and turn the shroud away from the bolt handle (counter clockwise) using the nose until it engages. Check it is firmly secured in the bolt.
Bolt: insert it at the back of the receiver, press the bolt catch on the left side down, and slide the bolt fully in. Turn the bolt until it returns to its closed position.
Magazine: confirm it is the right one for your caliber — the type and calibers are marked on its side — then insert it from below until the release button engages with an audible click.
Before the first shot: chamber and bore freed of oil and dried.
fncheck: Rifle unloaded, no cartridge in chamber or magazine. Safety on the white forward dot: the bolt is locked and will not open. Middle dot: the bolt handle lifts and the bolt opens, and the rifle cannot fire. With the safety on the forward dot, the trigger should move smoothly — Mauser names gummy oil and dirt as the cause of malfunctions here. The shroud must sit firmly in the bolt.
